subject.title: Feature: post-process NO_REPLY to suppress partial leaks

question: Should OpenClaw broaden `NO_REPLY` suppression for mixed trailing or own-line payloads, and what boundary should separate silent-intent internal text from legitimate substantive replies that append or mention the token?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally preserve some trailing-token replies, while the issue asks for broader suppression to prevent internal text leaks; changing that shared delivery contract requires maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Adopt a shared classifier
options.body: Define a single silent-intent classifier that suppresses internal/status preambles while preserving legitimate substantive replies, then apply it across the delivery surfaces.

options.title: Use blanket trailing suppression
options.body: Suppress any reply ending with an own-line or trailing `NO_REPLY`, accepting that some currently visible substantive replies may be dropped.

options.title: Keep the narrow contract
options.body: Document that only token-only, punctuation-wrapped token-only, and reasoning-prefixed silent payloads are suppressed, and close broad mixed-content suppression as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Adopt a shared classifier
recommendation.body: Define a single silent-intent classifier that suppresses internal/status preambles while preserving legitimate substantive replies, then apply it across the delivery surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: They landed the current mixed strip-and-deliver behavior and are the clearest routing owner for the shared reply-delivery policy decision.
